elements.element: The renewal structure must be either renewal only by mutual written agreement or automatic renewal.
elements.evidence: The clause uses automatic renewal for additional one-year terms.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, each renewal term must be 12 months.
elements.evidence: The clause provides for automatic renewal for additional “1-year terms.”

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Customer must be able to opt out of each renewal on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Although the clause mentions electing not to renew on 30 days' written notice, the right applies only “following the Initial Term” and is not clearly tied to a deadline before each renewal. It therefore does not clearly permit Customer to prevent the first automatic renewal.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Vendor must remind Customer 60 days before each renewal.
Any renewal price increase must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no restriction on renewal price increases.
The clause automatically renews for additional one-year terms.

elements.element: Customer's non-renewal notice requirement must be no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: The clause states 30 days, but the right is available only “following the Initial Term” and does not clearly establish a pre-renewal notice deadline that allows Customer to prevent the first automatic renewal.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must not exceed 5%.

result.reason: Neither level is complete. The redline preserves automatic one-year renewals and attempts to give Customer a 30-day non-renewal right, but the “following the Initial Term” trigger does not clearly allow notice that prevents the first renewal. It also omits the preferred 60-day reminder and both required price caps. The changes are confined to the relevant termination/non-renewal sentence and do not disturb unrelated breach or insolvency rights, but they do not reach a complete preferred or fallback position.
